description: The image displays three pie charts labeled “easy,” “medium,” and “hard,” each illustrating the distribution of performance outcomes for a Zero-Shot evaluation across four categories: N+K+, N−K+, N−K−, and N+K−, as defined in the legend. The “easy” chart shows N+K+ (teal) at 55.4%, N−K+ (yellow) at 38.3%, N−K− (orange) at 4.6%, and N+K− (red) at 1.7%. The “medium” chart shows N+K+ (teal) at 58.8%, N−K+ (yellow) at 35.4%, N−K− (orange) at 4.0%, and N+K− (red) at 1.8%. The “hard” chart shows N−K+ (yellow) at 37.3%, N−K− (orange) at 37.9%, N+K+ (teal) at 18.1%, and N+K− (red) at 6.7%. All charts use color-coded slices with percentage labels inside each segment, and the legend on the right maps colors to the four outcome categories. The visual progression suggests that as task difficulty increases from easy to hard, the proportion of successful outcomes (N+K+) decreases, while the proportion of outcomes where knowledge is absent but the model still performs well (N−K+) or fails (N−K−) increases.
